longdesc:
Configure an NFS server. Requires an existing file system resource,
for example a file system running on LVM on DRBD.
name: nfsserver

parameters.longdesc: The ID of an existing file system resource.
parameters.name: base-id

steps.longdesc:
Exportfs uses the exportfs command to add/remove nfs exports. It does
NOT manage the nfs server daemon. It depends on Linux specific NFS
implementation details, so is considered not portable to other
platforms yet.
steps.name: rootfs

parameters.longdesc: Cluster Resource ID
parameters.name: id

parameters.longdesc:
The client specification allowing remote machines to mount the
directory (or directories) over NFS.

Note: it follows the format defined in "man exportfs". For example, in
the use case to export the directory(-ies) for multiple subnets,
please do config a dedicated primitive for each subnet CIDR ip
address, and do not attempt to use multiple CIDR ip addresses in a
space separated list, like in /etc/exports.
parameters.name: clientspec

parameters.longdesc:
Any additional options to be given to the mount command, for example
rw,mountpoint
parameters.name: options

parameters.longdesc: The mount point for the file system, e.g.: /srv/nfs/home
parameters.name: directory

parameters.longdesc:
The fsid option to pass to exportfs. This can be a unique positive
integer, a UUID (assuredly sans comma characters), or the special
string "root" which is functionally identical to numeric fsid of 0. If
multiple directories are being exported, then they are assigned ids
sequentially starting with this fsid (fsid, fsid+1, fsid+2, ...).
Obviously, in that case the fsid must be an integer. 0 (root)
identifies the export as the root of an NFSv4 pseudofilesystem --
avoid this setting unless you understand its special status. This
value will override any fsid provided via the options parameter.
parameters.name: fsid
parameters.shortdesc: Unique FSID Within Cluster or Starting FSID for Multiple Exports

parameters.longdesc:
Relinquish NFS locks associated with this filesystem when the
resource stops. Enabling this parameter is highly recommended unless
the path exported by this exportfs resource is also exported by a
different resource.

Note: Unlocking is only possible on Linux systems where
/proc/fs/nfsd/unlock_filesystem exists and is writable. If your system
does not fulfill this requirement (on account of having an nonrecent
kernel, for example), you may set this parameter to 0 to silence the
associated warning.
parameters.name: unlock_on_stop

parameters.longdesc: If set to true, wait for lease on stop.
parameters.name: wait_for_leasetime_on_stop
parameters.shortdesc: Wait for Lease Time on Stop

parameters.longdesc:
Back up those entries from the NFS rmtab that apply to the exported
directory, to the specified backup file. The filename is interpreted
as relative to the exported directory. This backup is required if
clients are connecting to the export via NFSv3 over TCP. Note that a
configured monitor operation is required for this functionality.

To disable rmtab backups, set this parameter to the special string
"none".
parameters.name: rmtab_backup
parameters.shortdesc: Location of the rmtab backup, relative to directory.

steps.longdesc:
This Linux-specific resource manages IP alias IP addresses. It can
add an IP alias, or remove one. In addition, it can implement Cluster
Alias IP functionality if invoked as a clone resource.

If used as a clone, "shared address with a trivial, stateless
(autonomous) load-balancing/mutual exclusion on ingress" mode gets
applied (as opposed to "assume resource uniqueness" mode otherwise).
In that case, you should explicitly set clone-node-max >= 2, and/or
clone-max < number of nodes. In case of node failure, clone instances
need to be re-allocated on surviving nodes. This would not be possible
if there is already an instance on those nodes, and clone-node-max=1
(which is the default).

When the specified IP address gets assigned to a respective interface,
the resource agent sends unsolicited ARP (Address Resolution Protocol,
IPv4) or NA (Neighbor Advertisement, IPv6) packets to inform
neighboring machines about the change. This functionality is
controlled for both IPv4 and IPv6 by shared 'arp_*' parameters.
steps.name: virtual-ip

parameters.longdesc:
The IPv4 (dotted quad notation) or IPv6 address (colon hexadecimal
notation) example IPv4 "192.168.1.1". example IPv6
"2001:db8:DC28:0:0:FC57:D4C8:1FFF".
parameters.name: ip

parameters.longdesc:
The base network interface on which the IP address will be brought
online.  If left empty, the script will try and determine this from
the routing table.

Do NOT specify an alias interface in the form eth0:1 or anything here;
rather, specify the base interface only. If you want a label, see the
iflabel parameter.

Prerequisite:

There must be at least one static IP address, which is not managed by
the cluster, assigned to the network interface. If you can not assign
any static IP address on the interface, modify this kernel parameter:

sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.promote_secondaries=1 # (or per device)
parameters.name: nic

parameters.longdesc:
The netmask for the interface in CIDR format (e.g., 24 and not
255.255.255.0)

If unspecified, the script will also try to determine this from the
routing table.
parameters.name: cidr_netmask

parameters.longdesc:
Broadcast address associated with the IP. It is possible to use the
special symbols '+' and '-' instead of the broadcast address. In this
case, the broadcast address is derived by setting/resetting the host
bits of the interface prefix.
parameters.name: broadcast

parameters.longdesc: Proto to match when finding network. E.g. "kernel".
parameters.name: proto

parameters.longdesc:
You can specify an additional label for your IP address here. This
label is appended to your interface name.

The kernel allows alphanumeric labels up to a maximum length of 15
characters including the interface name and colon (e.g.
eth0:foobar1234)

A label can be specified in nic parameter but it is deprecated. If a
label is specified in nic name, this parameter has no effect.
parameters.name: iflabel

parameters.longdesc:
Enable support for LVS Direct Routing configurations. In case a IP
address is stopped, only move it to the loopback device to allow the
local node to continue to service requests, but no longer advertise it
on the network.

Notes for IPv6: It is not necessary to enable this option on IPv6.
Instead, enable 'lvs_ipv6_addrlabel' option for LVS-DR usage on IPv6.
parameters.name: lvs_support

parameters.longdesc:
Enable adding IPv6 address label so IPv6 traffic originating from the
address's interface does not use this address as the source. This is
necessary for LVS-DR health checks to realservers to work. Without it,
the most recently added IPv6 address (probably the address added by
IPaddr2) will be used as the source address for IPv6 traffic from that
interface and since that address exists on loopback on the
realservers, the realserver response to pings/connections will never
leave its loopback. See RFC3484 for the detail of the source address
selection.

See also 'lvs_ipv6_addrlabel_value' parameter.
parameters.name: lvs_ipv6_addrlabel

parameters.longdesc:
Specify IPv6 address label value used when 'lvs_ipv6_addrlabel' is
enabled. The value should be an unused label in the policy table which
is shown by 'ip addrlabel list' command. You would rarely need to
change this parameter.
parameters.name: lvs_ipv6_addrlabel_value

parameters.longdesc:
Set the interface MAC address explicitly. Currently only used in case
of the Cluster IP Alias. Leave empty to chose automatically.
parameters.name: mac

parameters.longdesc:
Firewall backend to use for cluster match rules: auto (default), nft
or iptables. The clusterip_table and clusterip_chain parameters apply
only to iptables; with nft a dedicated table per cluster IP is created
automatically.
parameters.name: clusterip_firewall

parameters.longdesc:
Specify the seed value of the hash used for the Cluster IP
functionality. If not specified, the value is computed from the IP
address, netmask and broadcast address.
parameters.name: clusterip_hash_seed

parameters.longdesc: The iptables table to use for the cluster match rules.
parameters.name: clusterip_table

parameters.longdesc: The iptables chain to use for the cluster match rules.
parameters.name: clusterip_chain

parameters.longdesc:
If true, use arptables to mangle ARP responses so that the cluster IP
address resolves to the multicast MAC address. Not supported for IPv6.
parameters.name: clusterip_mac_mangle
parameters.shortdesc: Mangle ARP responses for cluster MAC

parameters.longdesc:
If true, add the clone ID to the supplied value of IP to create a
unique address to manage
parameters.name: unique_clone_address
parameters.shortdesc: Create a unique address for cloned instances

parameters.longdesc:
Specify the interval between unsolicited ARP (IPv4) or NA (IPv6)
packets in milliseconds.

This parameter is deprecated and used for the backward compatibility
only. It is effective only for the send_arp binary which is built with
libnet, and send_ua for IPv6. It has no effect for other arp_sender.
parameters.name: arp_interval

parameters.longdesc:
Number of unsolicited ARP (IPv4) or NA (IPv6) packets to send at
resource initialization.
parameters.name: arp_count
parameters.shortdesc: ARP/NA packet count sent during initialization

parameters.longdesc:
For IPv4, number of unsolicited ARP packets to send during resource
monitoring. Doing so helps mitigate issues of stuck ARP caches
resulting from split-brain situations.
parameters.name: arp_count_refresh
parameters.shortdesc: ARP packet count sent during monitoring

parameters.longdesc:
Whether or not to send the ARP (IPv4) or NA (IPv6) packets in the
background. The default is true for IPv4 and false for IPv6.
parameters.name: arp_bg

parameters.longdesc:
For IPv4, the program to send ARP packets with on start. Available
options are:  - send_arp: default  - ipoibarping: default for
infiniband interfaces if ipoibarping is available  - iputils_arping:
use arping in iputils package  - libnet_arping: use another variant of
arping based on libnet
parameters.name: arp_sender

parameters.longdesc:
For IPv4, extra options to pass to the arp_sender program. Available
options are vary depending on which arp_sender is used.

A typical use case is specifying '-A' for iputils_arping to use ARP
REPLY instead of ARP REQUEST as Gratuitous ARPs.
parameters.name: send_arp_opts

parameters.longdesc:
Flush the routing table on stop. This is for applications which use
the cluster IP address and which run on the same physical host that
the IP address lives on. The Linux kernel may force that application
to take a shortcut to the local loopback interface, instead of the
interface the address is really bound to. Under those circumstances,
an application may, somewhat unexpectedly, continue to use connections
for some time even after the IP address is deconfigured. Set this
parameter in order to immediately disable said shortcut when the IP
address goes away.
parameters.name: flush_routes
parameters.shortdesc: Flush kernel routing table on stop

parameters.longdesc: For IPv4, whether or not to run arping for collision detection check.
parameters.name: run_arping
parameters.shortdesc: Run arping for IPv4 collision detection check

parameters.longdesc:
For IPv6, do not perform Duplicate Address Detection when adding the
address.
parameters.name: nodad

parameters.longdesc: Use noprefixroute flag (see 'man ip-address').
parameters.name: noprefixroute

parameters.longdesc:
For IPv6, set the preferred lifetime of the IP address. This can be
used to ensure that the created IP address will not be used as a
source address for routing. Expects a value as specified in section
5.5.4 of RFC 4862.
parameters.name: preferred_lft

parameters.longdesc:
Specifies the network namespace to operate within. The namespace must
already exist, and the interface to be used must be within the
namespace.
parameters.name: network_namespace

parameters.longdesc:
Consider the resource failed if the interface has status DOWN or
LOWERLAYERDOWN.
parameters.name: check_link_status
parameters.shortdesc: Consider the resource failed if the interface has status DOWN or LOWERLAYERDOWN
